Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "lowercase please make a small python function for our log-file cleanup utility. it gets called from another module, so take a folder, a cutoff date, and a confirm_delete flag as arguments. the folder has rotated web-service logs and sometimes .log.gz files too; only consider files ending in .log. match files whose modification time is earlier than the cutoff, not ones with the same time. if confirm_delete is true, delete the matching .log files, but only in that case. if it’s false, don’t delete anything; instead return the matching paths as a preview so i can check what would be removed. the preview should use the same set of files as the delete branch, and if there are no matches it should just be an empty list. keep it focused on this function, use the standard library, and don’t add a command line interface. return only the function, no explanation or examples. i want to be able to review the preview before connecting the function to the rest of the cleanup utility.", "output": "Write a small Python function for a log-file cleanup utility. The function will be called from another module, so give it arguments for a folder, a cutoff date, and a `confirm_delete` flag.

Consider only files ending in `.log`; ignore `.log.gz` files. A file matches when its modification time is earlier than the cutoff, not equal to it.

- If `confirm_delete` is true, delete the matching `.log` files.
- Otherwise, do not delete anything; return the matching paths as a preview.

Use the same matching files for the preview and deletion branches. If there are no matches, return an empty list in preview mode. Keep the implementation focused on this function and use the standard library. Do not add a command-line interface.

Return only the function, without explanation or examples."}]
